correctness.rationale: Assume every vertex has degree 1 or 2, and utility same-coalition neighbors divided by total coalition size. A stable partition cannot give any vertex zero internal neighbors (move to a neighbor gives positive utility). On a crossing edge vw, each endpoint has exactly one internal friend and one external friend, so nonimprovement in both directions forces ||A|−|B||≤1. Conversely each vertex with two internal friends has no profitable outside move, and each vertex with one has at most one external friend, to whose coalition payoff 1/(|B|+1)≤1/|A| under size balance. Thus criterion works even if coalitions disconnected; singleton creation never improves. For C_n, a coalition of t≥2 runs needs each run and each gap length≥2, hence n≥4t. Alternating two coalitions in runs length≥2 with size difference≤1 attains t=floor(n/4). At n=8 exactly two distinct stable labeled partitions have disconnected coalition. Exact small-n independent exhaustive partition calculations confirmed counts 1,3,6,6,15,17 through n=8 and 2 disconnected n=8; infinite proof is structural.
